_comment: TEMPLATE for the server catalog. Copy to servers.json and describe YOUR machines there. servers.json is SITE configuration: it names a deployment's machines, so it is gitignored and never committed. Distribute an edited catalog to every host with `fw fleet servers --push`; give a new host its first copy with `setup-ubuntu-fleet-host.sh --catalog FILE`. Machines are listed by STABLE NAME (mDNS/DNS), never by IP, and resolved at startup/reconcile time, so DHCP drift heals on the next resolution. Per-host override: servers.local.json (merged over servers.json by name; top-level "_remove": [...] drops entries). See docs/reference/server-catalog.md. Rules of thumb: (1) 'name' is a STABLE resolvable name — mDNS .local on a single LAN, or a real DNS name; consumers resolve it to the current IP at startup/reconcile, which is what makes DHCP drift a non-event. (2) 'aliases' are the conventional service names other config refers to (afl-mongodb, afl-minio, ...) — they map to this machine without /etc/hosts entries. (3) exactly one entry should have 'infra': true — the machine running MongoDB/MinIO/dashboard; tools use it as the default infra target. (4) 'ip_pin' is a LAST RESORT for hosts that name resolution cannot reach (cross-subnet, no mDNS): a pinned IP goes stale when the lease changes, which is the failure this catalog removes — leave it null if you can. 'group' is the FW_SERVER_GROUP role tag used by server-groups gating (docs/architecture/server-groups.md).

_groups.heavy: Enough memory for the largest OSM cut (a europe split has peaked at 18.9 GB) AND hundreds of GB of scratch. Runs every role, including osm-geocoder/osm-lz/gh-router.
_groups.medium: Enough memory for every domain role, but not the scratch headroom for OSM staging. osm-geocoder/gh-router are gated away.
_groups.runner: The light tier and the default for a host whose capacity has not been measured: ffl orchestration + one generalist runner.

_services.afl-extracts: The self-hosted OSM extract server. osmosis_replication_base_url is stamped from this alias, so it must follow the host that actually serves the tree.
_services.afl-registry: The fleet image registry (host:5050). `fw fleet rollout` and `fw fleet agent-image` push here.
_services.afl-backup: Where `fw maint backup-mongo` writes archives. Never the database host.
_services._note: Each afl-* service resolves to the entry whose aliases claim it; a service no entry claims falls back to the "infra": true host (the one-box default). `fw fleet servers --service-host afl-registry` prints the answer.

servers.name: infra-host.local
servers.purpose: infra: object store, PostGIS, dashboard, image registry

servers.name: db-host.local
servers.purpose: MongoDB control plane + OSM extract server + heavy runner tier

servers.name: light-host.local
servers.purpose: light runner tier: ffl orchestration + one generalist runner; also holds Mongo backups
